dialogues.speaker: Kholmogorov
dialogues.text: Now, I'm certain I have that photo in my bag somewhere... Hm. No, I can't seem to find it. That's a shame. I really wanted to show them to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kholmogorov
dialogues.text: My son and his family moved back to Novokitezhgrad for work. We used to live there too, back when he was just a boy... Oh, listen to me — I've already told you that, haven't I? Now then, what was I saying?

dialogues.speaker: Chagina
dialogues.text: You were telling me about your grandson's birthday. Please, go on. I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Kholmogorov
dialogues.text: Ah, yes! His birthday, of course. Tell me, do you think he'd like a toy from Snezhnograd? Human craftsmen do fine work too, you know, every bit as good as ours.

dialogues.speaker: Chagina
dialogues.text: If he's grown up in Novokitezhgrad, he must have a good eye. Still, I'm sure he wouldn't mind a toy made by human hands. It'd be something new for him at least, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Kholmogorov
dialogues.text: Oh, yes. You're right. That does put my mind at ease now.

dialogues.speaker: Kholmogorov
dialogues.text: I can't wait to see him. I wonder if he's grown a bit taller... Ah, I wish I had his photo with me. He has such a sweet smile.

dialogues.speaker: Chagina
dialogues.text: I'm sure he does. I can tell from the way you smile whenever you talk about him. But sir, if you want to see him soon, you'd better get on your train.

dialogues.speaker: Kholmogorov
dialogues.text: My train... Ah, yes, that's right. I'm taking the train to Novokitezhgrad. Where do I get on?

dialogues.speaker: Chagina
dialogues.text: Please don't worry, sir. Everything's been arranged. I'll take you to the train in a little while, and there'll be someone onboard to take care of you too.

dialogues.speaker: Chagina
dialogues.text: Once you arrive in Novokitezhgrad, all you have to do is to wait at the Transport Bureau office. The folks there will get in touch with your family and make sure they come get you.
